hero.title: Rabindranath Tagore University
hero.summary: Rabindranath Tagore University’s Faculty of Agriculture began undergraduate teaching in 2015-16 in Raisen district near Bhopal. Its four-year agriculture programme links crop and soil science with rural work, agricultural enterprises and a research farm supported by irrigation and machinery.

overview.heading: Agriculture teaching with a rural development context
paragraphs: RNTU’s agriculture faculty describes its original purpose as expanding agricultural education in underserved parts of Raisen district. The degree began in 2015-16. The current course account covers agronomy, horticulture, soil science, plant health, breeding, economics and extension, bringing production science and the social setting of farming into the same undergraduate route.

The published programme structure includes village surveys, soil sampling, plant-protection interventions and agro-industrial attachment. It also lists enterprise learning options such as beekeeping, mushroom cultivation and seed production. These are curriculum descriptions; applicants should ask which modules will actually run for their cohort and how the practical timetable is organised.

faqs.question: When did RNTU’s agriculture degree begin?
faqs.answer: The faculty account dates the four-year programme to the 2015-16 academic session.

faqs.question: Which 12th backgrounds does the course page list?
faqs.answer: PCM, PCB, PCMB or Agriculture, with a stated 60% threshold for general and reserved categories. Confirm intake applicability.

faqs.question: Does Shiksha Mitra automatically cover agriculture?
faqs.answer: No. The displayed 2022 scheme on the admissions page specifically excludes B.Sc. Agriculture.

faqs.question: What enterprise options appear in the curriculum?
faqs.answer: The course page lists options including beekeeping, mushrooms and seed-production technology; availability for each cohort needs confirmation.

faqs.question: What is the checked ICAR term?
faqs.answer: The Faculty of Agriculture’s B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture row runs from 8 February 2024 to 7 February 2029.
